about.title: Montclair Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Montclair sees steady foot traffic near its retail corridors and residential complexes off Monte Vista Avenue and Central Avenue, and with that traffic comes the occasional wet floor, broken step, or poorly lit stairwell that a property owner should have caught. California law doesn't hand you a win just because you fell; you generally need to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why documenting the scene matters as much as the injury itself. Photos of the hazard, names of witnesses, and store or building surveillance footage can disappear fast if no one asks for them. Our team handles slip and fall cases throughout Montclair and understands how to gather this evidence and evaluate a claim under a contingency arrangement, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Montclair, it costs nothing to find out where you stand.

items.title: We Help Establish Notice
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Our team can help track down maintenance logs, inspection records, and prior complaints that show notice existed.

items.title: Video Doesn't Wait, and Neither Should You
items.desc: Many Montclair businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Contacting us quickly can mean the difference between having that footage preserved or losing it forever.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present your side clearly instead of letting an insurer assign you most of the blame.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Montclair?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government entity, like the City of Montclair, owns or maintains the property, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's worth confirming your timeline with our team as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Central Avenue or Holt Boulevard and no one else saw it happen?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't end a claim, but it does make evidence more important. Store surveillance cameras, incident reports, and photos you take of the hazard right after the fall can carry the case even without a bystander account.

items.question: Will the property owner's insurance company just believe what happened?
items.answer: Insurers typically investigate on their own timeline and often look for reasons to reduce or deny a payout. That's part of why documenting the hazard immediately and speaking with our team early can help make sure your version of events is backed by evidence, not just your word.
